name: Siem Reap
tagline: Angkor is the anchor; Cambodia is the trip
summary: Make Siem Reap a multi-day base rather than a sunrise photo stop. Split Angkor’s major temples across days and leave time for Khmer food, craft workshops and context in town.
seasonNote: Dry-season mornings are comfortable but popular; April is extremely hot and wet-season storms change the feel of the temples.
arrival: Siem Reap–Angkor International Airport is far from town; pre-arrange a transfer and allow a generous arrival buffer.
gettingAround: Hire a licensed driver or tuk-tuk for temple circuits; negotiate a complete itinerary and hours.
cashTip: Many visitor prices are quoted in USD; carry clean small notes and expect riel change. These app budgets are in USD.
foodTip: Try fish amok and Khmer curries; ask about fish sauce and prahok when choosing vegetarian meals.
buyTip: Choose textiles, carvings and crafts from transparent workshops; do not buy antiquities.
baseArea: Central Siem Reap with a quiet side street.

connections.note: Approximate flight time; airport transfer is substantial.

sources.title: Tripadvisor visitor favourites and review snapshots

reviewSummary: Visitor accounts support allowing several visits across the temple complex rather than rushing everything into one day. Official passes are USD 37 for one day, 62 for three days and 72 for seven days at the research date.

items.name: Angkor Wat
items.summary: The great temple complex that anchors a Cambodia visit.
items.expect: Long walks, stairs, heat and dense sunrise crowds.
items.tip: Buy the official pass and plan your circuit; the same pass covers other included Angkor temples.
items.priceNote: Official pass snapshot checked 2026-11-04: USD 37 one day, 62 three days, 72 seven days. Buy once; do not add again for each included temple.

review.note: Dated indexed review snapshot; review count is a popularity proxy, not measured footfall.

whyVisit: The great temple complex that anchors a Cambodia visit.
Moats, galleries and towers reveal the scale and planning of the Khmer temple landscape.
visitFlow: Use a valid official Angkor pass and a realistic route.
Choose one major relief gallery and the permitted upper areas rather than rushing.
tradeoffs: Long walks, stairs, heat and dense sunrise crowds.
